data.title: NextCure Received Notice of Noncompliance
data.description:
On November 16, 2026, NextCure received notice from Nasdaq that its stockholders’ equity of $5.503 million was below the $10 million minimum required by Listing Rule 5450(b)(1)(A), and it did not meet alternative compliance standards. The company has until January 4, 2027, to submit a plan to regain compliance, but expects its proposed merger with Avere Therapeutics to close before then and potentially resolve the issue; trading continues on Nasdaq in the meantime.

Original SEC Filing: NextCure, Inc. [ NXTC ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: FirstEnergy Raises 2026–2030 Core Earnings Growth Outlook to 7%–9%, Investment Plan to $38 Billion
data.description:
FirstEnergy raised its 2026–2030 Core Earnings per share growth outlook to 7%–9% and increased its capital investment plan to $38 billion.

Key Highlights:

  • West Virginia regulators approved construction of the Maidsville combined-cycle natural gas facility and a surcharge for cash recovery of financing costs during construction.
  • The 2026–2030 investment plan rises from $36 billion to $38 billion, including about $2 billion for Maidsville.
  • FirstEnergy plans to fund approximately 35% of Maidsville’s investment with equity or equity-like securities, raising anticipated 2026–2030 equity financing needs to $2.8 billion from $2.0 billion.
  • The company increased its long-term Core Earnings per share CAGR outlook from 6%–8% to 7%–9%, targeting the upper half of the range.
  • The updated plan projects 11.1% rate base CAGR, up from 10.4%.

Original SEC Filing: FIRSTENERGY CORP [ FE ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Singapore's banks carry more AI data-centre risk than Japan's megabanks
data.description:
Singapore's three big banks have put between 3% and 5% of their loan books into data centres, roughly double the share at Japan's two largest lenders, research house CreditSights estimates.

In a report dated November 16, the Fitch Solutions-owned firm counted $20.7bn of direct data-centre financing at Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), or 1.8% of its credit exposure, and $16.3bn, or 1.9%, at Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG). American lenders typically hold about 2% of loans or less in the sector.

Those are modest numbers, and the banks lean on them. The sharper danger from a cooling AI cycle lies in the fee business lenders have built around arranging data-centre debt and selling most of it on. A slowdown would dent fee growth before it produced credit losses, according to CreditSights, and an underwriting commitment turns into balance-sheet risk the moment investors stop taking the paper as fast as planned. The borrowers are meanwhile spending faster than they earn.

Data-centre financing as a share of credit exposure (Japan) or total loans (US, Singapore). Source: CreditSights report of November 16, 2026; OCBC. IntelliNews

Tokyo sells it on

MUFG's own interim investor presentation puts its data-centre exposure at $20.8bn at the end of August, about JPY3.3 trillion at today's rate. Of that, 57% sits in the Americas, 19% in Asia, 14% in Japan and 10% in Europe. The bank passed on roughly 70% of its share of the data-centre project-finance deals it arranged between April and August to other investors, and about 90% on gigawatt-scale transactions.

SMFG is pulling back harder. 'This year we have adopted stricter standards on extending credit for data centre financing, for instance restricting ourselves to just hyperscalers with high credit standing,' chief executive Toru Nakashima told a press briefing on November 13, Reuters reported. He warned that a slowdown in data-centre investment could weigh on the group's results over the next six months.

The group's results presentation shows JPY2.1 trillion ($13.1bn) of data-centre project finance inside total exposure of JPY177 trillion. Hyperscalers are the off-takers on 80% of it, and SMFG sold down about 90% of the US data-centre project finance it originated in the year to September, against about 70% a year earlier. Mizuho Financial Group chief executive Masahiro Kihara named tougher curbs on US data-centre construction after the Democrats' midterm gains as a tail risk.

MUFG data-centre exposure by region at end-August 2026, % of $20.8bn. Source: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group interim investor presentation. IntelliNews

Singapore lends next door

Singapore's lenders sit closer to the region's construction boom. DBS, OCBC and UOB were among seven banks behind DayOne's MYR15bn ($3.6bn) Johor package in October, and the three jointly arranged a SGD5bn ($3.9bn) loan backing KKR and Singtel's purchase of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres. The same trio was picked to run the Singapore-dollar tranche of Alphabet's planned debut Asian bond sale in November, the kind of fee income CreditSights expects the AI build-out to keep generating.

OCBC chief executive Tan Teck Long put data-centre lending at below 3% of a SGD372bn ($288bn) loan book at third-quarter results, with AI-related exposure under 1%, The Asian Banker reported. He prefers projects backed by established hyperscalers, with power supply and customers signed before any money is lent.

Spending ahead of the cash

Tencent shows how quickly the borrowers' arithmetic can shift. The Shenzhen-based group booked capital expenditures of CNY81.4bn ($12.2bn) in the third quarter, up from CNY52.8bn in the second and CNY13.0bn a year earlier, according to its results release. Free cash flow came to minus CNY69.1bn ($10.4bn), negative for a second quarter running, and net cash of CNY102.4bn a year ago has become net debt of CNY13.7bn.

Tencent attributes most of the outflow to prepayments for computing capacity, without which free cash flow would have been a positive CNY16.9bn. Cash actually paid out for capital expenditures was CNY65.1bn, its results presentation shows.

Tencent capital expenditures and free cash flow by quarter, CNY bn. Source: Tencent Holdings results releases and presentations. IntelliNews

Exposure that never shows up as a data-centre loan is harder to count. CreditSights singles out lending to private credit funds and technology companies as the hardest channel to measure, and expects regulators to scrutinise AI-related financing more closely as it grows. SMFG alone reports JPY10.5 trillion ($65.6bn) of financing to funds, though it says the borrowers are mostly investment grade and none of the loans has soured.

Big tech's build-out is increasingly paid for with borrowed money, from Tencent's swing into net debt to Alphabet's Singapore-dollar bonds, and arranging that debt feeds the banks' fee lines. Should investors balk, perhaps over the leadership turmoil at Nvidia, the first casualty would be the pipeline of deals that pays for Asian banks' investment-banking teams. A slower pipeline would leave more of the debt sitting on their balance sheets.

At that point Singapore's 3-5% looks a good deal less comfortable than Tokyo's 2%.

data.title: House Democrats Reportedly Probe Whether Nvidia Tried To Influence US Investigation Into Megaspeed
data.description:
Key points:
  • Two House Democrats have opened an inquiry into whether Nvidia sought to influence the Commerce Department’s investigation of Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed.
  • Representatives Gregory Meeks (D-NY) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) have asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to provide answers and relevant documents by December 1.
  • The report said Nvidia contacted Commerce investigators in August 2025 after the department had requested records on the company’s sales to Megaspeed.

Two House Democrats have reportedly opened an inquiry into whether Nvidia (NVDA) sought to influence the Commerce Department’s investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud company suspected of illegally diverting advanced chips to China.

According to a Reuters report, Representatives Gregory Meeks (D-NY), ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) sent a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Thursday seeking answers and relevant documents by December 1.

The lawmakers want to know whether the Commerce Department allowed a major U.S. company with financial and personal ties to the Trump administration to interfere in an enforcement matter.

NVDA stock was down 2% in pre-market trade, on track to log a seven-day losing streak. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ levels of chatter.

Nvidia and Megaspeed had not responded to Stocktwits’ request for comment at the time of writing.

Democrats Question Nvidia’s Contact With Commerce Investigators

“The U.S. public and Congress deserve a full accounting of what happened,” the lawmakers wrote, according to Reuters.

The inquiry centers in part on Nvidia’s communications with Commerce Department investigators. Reuters reported that Nvidia contacted department employees directly in August 2025 and requested a meeting with one of them. The company reportedly told the employees that Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler had authorized it to communicate with them.

The contact came after Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia in May 2025 concerning sales to Megaspeed. The following month, U.S. investigators, working with Singaporean authorities, conducted an on-site inspection at the cloud company.

Megaspeed, Nvidia Investigation Timeline

The Commerce Department began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 over potential export-control violations, according to a joint statement from the Commerce and Justice departments earlier this week. Nvidia later placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, the statement said. The Justice Department subsequently took the lead in the criminal investigation.

Nvidia told Reuters that, as an American company, it consults with Commerce officials to provide information, answer questions and seek guidance. The company added that it looks forward to “engaging with Congress on this matter.”

The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security said it conducts enforcement “strictly by the book,” according to Reuters. Megaspeed told Reuters that it complies with all applicable laws, including U.S. export-control requirements.

Nvidia Faces Wider Congressional Scrutiny Ahead Of December Interviews

The latest inquiry comes amid broader congressional scrutiny of Nvidia, its sales of advanced chips and the Commerce Department’s handling of suspected diversion to China.

On Tuesday, representatives Jamie Raskin (D-MD), Meeks and Kamlager-Dove sent a separate letter to Brandon Lutnick, chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald, seeking records related to the firm’s Nvidia holdings and its business interests in China and Southeast Asia.

The lawmakers also questioned whether Commerce Secretary Lutnick’s decisions on export controls may have been influenced by the firm’s financial interests. The letter was addressed to Brandon Lutnick, not the Commerce Secretary.

Nvidia is also facing questions from House committees investigating whether Chinese actors obtained access to its advanced chips. Former CEO Jensen Huang agreed to a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on December 1. Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels on December 2.

Separately, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC), chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, has asked Huang to testify before the panel on December 3 and Lutnick to appear on December 10.

The House Energy and Commerce Committee has also opened its own inquiry. Chairman Brett Guthrie (R-KY) sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress on Wednesday, requesting a briefing by December 2 on the company’s role in the Megaspeed matter and its export-compliance controls.

Guthrie also sent separate letters to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler, seeking briefings on the department’s handling of the case.

The scrutiny now spans three separate congressional efforts.

data.title: Nasdaq futures slide as Anthropic retreat deepens AI jitters
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures down: Dow 0.1%, S&P 500 0.74%, Nasdaq 1.64%
  • Anthropic down 7.4% a day after debut
  • Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nasdaq futures fell more than 1% on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 7.4% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's earnings this week were seen as key tests of whether battered investor confidence in the AI trade could recover.

But neither revived enthusiasm after weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

As of Thursday's close, the Nasdaq was 13.6% below its October 6 record closing high, while the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX had posted its sixth consecutive loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon and Microsoft declined more than 1.5% each, while Meta fell 2% and Alphabet was muted. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Nvidia fell 2.2%, while Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Marvell , and Micron lost between 2.2% and 6.6%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped about 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN , Applied Digital and Core Scientific fell about 4% each.

At 7:03 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were down 48 points, or 0.1%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 53.5 points, or 0.74%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 436 points, or 1.64%.

The CBOE Volatility Index , Wall Street's fear gauge, hit the 30-point mark for the first time since March 30.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% beat analyst earnings expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 9.7% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

data.title: Danaher Collaborates with Microsoft to Make Scientific Instruments Agentically Connected and Laboratories More Intelligent
data.description:
Advancing autonomous science through smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Danaher Corporation () today announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft to support the development of smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem that connects technologies across Danaher while remaining open to the broader laboratory ecosystem, helping scientists move from scientific questions to experimental evidence faster. The partnership seeks to combine Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise with Microsoft's AI technologies, making experimental execution more streamlined and insights more readily available to translate discovery into human impact.

The partnership is focused on accelerating the development of a common agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation. The platform is built on Microsoft technology: Microsoft Azure for secure, compliant cloud infrastructure, and Microsoft Foundry to power the AI agents that interpret results and guide instrument control. Its goal is to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation, while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories.

While the companies are continuing to develop this platform, the first commercial applications will reach Danaher customers this year, including MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant, Molecular Devices' software for its high-content cellular imaging systems, designed to provide product support. Additional next-generation, agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use this platform are planned for 2027.

"Danaher's businesses bring deep scientific and instrument expertise to customers every day," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and CEO of Danaher. "With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher. Through context and learning, that foundation can continuously inform the next experiment and the best analysis. This partnership is an important step toward making laboratories not just connected, but intelligent."

As part of this partnership, smart, agent-enabled instruments are being designed with the goal of supporting scientists across four critical activities:

  • Translating scientific intent into experimental plans, instrument setup and methods
  • Controlling instrument hardware within defined safety boundaries and with user oversight, while guiding execution and troubleshooting
  • Interpreting results and identifying quality issues in real time
  • Recommending corrective actions and next experiments for scientist review

AI-assisted instruments are intended to simplify complex scientific workflows. In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists conducting an AI-assisted experiment on a Leica microscope took up to 83% less time and up to 68% fewer steps to complete than a novice working without the AI assistant, while producing high-quality data and completing the experiment in a time comparable to an expert.

"Danaher's scientific expertise, combined with Microsoft's AI platform, aims to give scientists more choice and control, and more time for discovery," said Deb Cupp, Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer, Microsoft Global Enterprise. "This partnership aligns with our goal to help translate AI into real-world impact."

The partnership is designed to advance Danaher's broader strategy for AI and autonomous science by connecting intelligence at the instrument with data, laboratory workflows and the physical execution of experiments. Intelligent instruments are a first step. As instruments and laboratory systems become more connected and interoperable, Danaher believes experimental results can help scientists determine what to do next, supporting discovery through increasingly connected and autonomous workflows under scientific oversight.

data.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Traders Assess Supply Outlook, Middle East Risks — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices retreated Friday after earlier gains as traders assessed improving global supply conditions and continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments.

Brent crude futures fell 0.7% to $91.36 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate declined 1% to $82.40 a barrel.

Both benchmarks have fallen around 15% so far this month as U.S. President Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran. A stronger U.S. dollar and broader weakness across commodity markets have also added to pressure on oil prices.

Oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints rose 19% in the third quarter from the previous three months, according to a report published Thursday by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The agency said regional crude production reached 23.1 million barrels a day in October, the highest since the conflict began, as producers expand shipments through alternative routes. The EIA expects Brent to average $86 a barrel next year as recovering supplies help rebuild global inventories.

The agency said shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and Suez Canal increased, while flows through the Bab el-Mandeb declined. Preliminary shipping data from Vortexa indicated that shipments remained near third-quarter levels in October.

Steadily increasing oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz had contributed to the recent decline in crude prices, the EIA said. The agency expects global oil inventories to increase as Middle Eastern production and exports recover, while oil demand remains relatively flat in the near term.

The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Israel's spy chief had urged U.S. officials to support renewed strikes against Iran, while Gulf countries pressed for negotiations amid concerns about retaliatory attacks on regional infrastructure. President Trump is weighing whether to resume a broader military campaign against Tehran.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia said Thursday that a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh's financial district, with no injuries reported, according to the Saudi Press Agency. The Wall Street Journal identified the building as the headquarters of the kingdom's Public Investment Fund.

Pavel Molchanov, an investment strategist at Raymond James, said Thursday that oil markets have become increasingly accustomed to periodic tensions in the Middle East, provided they don't escalate into a broader conflict. He said production among OPEC's Persian Gulf members had recovered to 87% of prewar levels as the industry adapted to disruptions.

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that the response in oil prices to the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz had been less severe than the scale of the supply shock might have suggested, amid ample global supply and well-stocked inventories.

In its World Energy Outlook, the agency said the global oil market was expected to return to a surplus as Middle Eastern production recovered faster than demand. It projects an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to about 3.8 million barrels a day next year.

The agency also said prolonged disruptions to shipping through the strait could accelerate investment in alternative export routes, with around 7 million barrels a day of new pipeline capacity under construction or consideration. The projects would require an estimated $40 billion in investment, adding about $2 to the cost of each barrel of Middle Eastern oil exported.

data.title: The Container Store, A Neighborhood Intelligence Company, Announces Restoration of Its Systems Following Cybersecurity Incident
data.description:
Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc. () today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, The Container Store, has restored its website and systems following a cybersecurity incident this past weekend.

Upon detecting suspicious activity, the company immediately activated its established cybersecurity protocols and proactively suspended online order-taking at The Container Store to protect its customer information and its systems. All retail locations remained open, serving customers through alternative transaction-processing procedures.

Marcus Lemonis, Chief Executive Officer of Neighborhood Intelligence, commented:

“I am extremely proud of how our technology and operational teams responded. We made the deliberate decision to prioritize the protection of our customers and our systems while keeping our stores open and serving customers. Our established protocols, combined with the expertise of our outside partners, allowed us to respond with discipline and restore operations in a controlled manner. I want to thank our associates and partners for their exceptional work and our customers for their patience and continued support.”

As part of its established response protocols, the company engaged leading independent cybersecurity experts to assist with the investigation, containment and restoration efforts. Our investigation into this event is ongoing, however we do not believe that this incident impacted the security of any customer financial data because The Container Store does not store or maintain consumer financial or payment information.

The company also maintains established risk mitigation procedures and business interruption insurance coverage designed to help manage operational and financial exposure associated with incidents of this nature.

The incident was isolated to The Container Store. We expect a minimal impact on consolidated revenue for the quarter, with any impact on profitability expected to be mitigated by our business interruption insurance. The company’s other businesses, including Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY and Kirkland’s, remained unaffected. The company continues to expect sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

About Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc.

Neighborhood Intelligence (), previously Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc., is a data and technology company organized around three interconnected pillars: Omni-Channel Retail, Home Services and Home Ownership. Its portfolio includes Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY, Kirkland’s, The Container Store, Elfa and Closet Works, along with its expanding Home Services and Home Ownership businesses. data.title: Nvidia, AMD in focus as GF Securities says talk of server CPU cuts is 'overstated'
data.description:
Despite rumors that tech companies have started to cut orders for server CPUs, GF Securities said supply chain checks show just the opposite.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm said any talk that Meta and Microsoft have cut orders is inaccurate and that Meta has shifted some purchases of x86 to Nvidia's Grace and Vera server options. Additionally, Meta has accelerated general-server deployments for its Muse artificial intelligence agent.

For Microsoft, orders are unchanged, and any noise is simply reflecting original design manufacturer capacity allocations.

“Agentic workloads now account for ~80% of tokens on OpenRouter (weekly volume up 35x YoY), with GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol and Claude Duet supporting commercial adoption, while Meta Muse gained 11.2mn NA accounts in 7 weeks but saw Day-30 retention fall to 16.4%,” analysts at the firm wrote in a note to clients. “We maintain server CPU TAM of $211bn by 2030 (+47% CAGR), with 2027 unit growth of 29% (general servers +15%, AI-inference CPUs +79%) as agentic AI expands from 25% to 50% of total inference.”

The investment firm reiterated its Buy rating on AMD as it sees the Dr. Lisa Su-led company benefiting from a ramp in its Venice CPUs and continued share gains in x86 processors.

“We expect Venice to drive further share gains for AMD in the coming quarters, even outperforming Intel’s Diamond Rapids (set to launch by late 1Q27), on the back of superior perf-per-watt, large L3 SRAM, and up to 512 threads,” analysts at the firm added. “For now, we forecast Venice CPU shipments of 400k/5.4mn in 2026/2027, respectively.”

The firm also reiterated its Buy rating on Intel due to the company ramping up its Granite Rapids processors.
